# Elora Gorge

Section Menu

## Conservation Area Status

The total number of daily visitors to our conservation areas is limited and access may be restricted. Get [real-time capacity information](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/conservation-area-capacity-status/ "Conservation Area and Capacity status"), including whether the conservation area, or an activity, is open or has reached its operating capacity.

## Conservation Area Information

The Elora Gorge is one of the most beautiful and spectacular natural areas in the Grand River valley. The Grand River rushes past 22-metre high cliffs. Riverside trails (with safety barriers) and scenic overlooks provide hikers with stunning views of the water far below where kayakers and tubers make their way through the rapids.

**WARNING:** The gorge is deep, and the walls are steep. For your safety, hike only on marked trails. Stay away from the edge of the gorge. Do not climb over fences or attempt to climb down the gorge walls.

- **Season:** May 1 - October 15
- **Hours:** See real-time hours on our [Conservation Area Activity Status page](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/conservation-area-activity-status/#gsc.tab=0 "Conservation Area and Activity status").

  - The gatehouse may not be open during all conservation area operating hours. When the gatehouse is closed, please register and pay for your day use visit using the self-registration box.
  - Not all facilities are available during all conservation area operating hours.
- **Location:** 7400 Wellington County Road 21, Elora - [Google Map of conservation area location](https://www.google.ca/maps/place/43%C2%B040'10.2%22N+80%C2%B026'28.8%22W/@43.669491,-80.4435137,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m2!3m1!1s0x0:0x0?hl=en "Open new window to view google map of Elora Gorge location")
- **Notice:**
  - The low level bridge is closed to vehicles until further notice.
  - Elora Quarry admission tickets and vehicle permits are not valid for admission to the Elora Gorge Conservation Area. The [Elora Quarry Conservation Area](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-quarry/ "Elora Quarry") is a different property.
- [Conservation area fees](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/conservation-area-services-info-fees-and-more/conservation-area-fees/elora-gorge-fees/ "Elora Gorge Conservation Area Fees")
- [Tubing](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/tubing-at-elora-gorge/ "Tubing at Elora Gorge")

## Activities

[Camping](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_1)

**Campsites**: Elora Gorge Conservation Area has 450 campsites including; 250 unserviced sites, 130 serviced sites with water and 15/30 amp electrical, 20 serviced sites with 15 amp electrical, and 60 fully serviced sites with water, 15/30 amp electrical and sewer connection. Up to six people are permitted per campsite. Check-in is after 2 p.m. and check out is before noon.

- Please read our [Camping Reservation Policy](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/conservation-area-services-info-fees-and-more/camping-reservation-policy/ "Camping reservation policy")

**Group camping**: One group campsite is available for **registered youth groups only**.

**Seasonal sites**: Please see our [seasonal camping page](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/camping/seasonal-camping/ "Seasonal camping") for information on seasonal camp sites.

**Alcohol and Cannabis:** A total alcohol and cannabis ban is in effect for the entire season. Alcohol and cannabis are not permitted at any time, including on all registered campsites and in day-use areas.

[Canoeing](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_2)

The gorge offers a challenge to experienced whitewater kayakers. Canoeists like to start at the lower end of the conservation area and the Low Level Bridge for a trip downstream toward West Montrose (home of the famous covered bridge), Waterloo and Kitchener.

[Tubing](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_3)

Riding an inner tube through the Elora Gorge is an exhilarating way to experience the river and the cliffs above. Tubing may be closed due to high flows or other conditions. For more information about tubing, status updates and to purchase tickets online, please visit the **[Tubing](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/tubing-at-elora-gorge/ "Tubing at Elora Gorge")** page.

The shuttle bus for tubing is no longer in operation.

[Splash pad](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_4)

The 195-square-metre splash pad has 18 spray and splash features to keep kids cool on a hot summer day.

Elora Gorge Conservation Area doesn't have a swimming area.

[Fishing](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_5)

The stretch of the Grand River between Fergus and West Montrose, which includes the Elora Gorge, has attained a well-deserved reputation as one of the best brown trout fisheries in North America. Fishing enthusiasts generally wade in the river, although it is rocky and slippery in some areas. Wading cleats are recommended. **[Special fishing regulations](http://www.ontario.ca/document/2015-ontario-fishing-regulations-summary "Open new window to view Fishing Regulations in Ontario")** are in place along some sections of the Grand River.

Go to our **[Fishing](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/fishing/ "Fishing")** page for more information on fishing in the Grand River watershed.

[Hiking](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_6)

There are two kilometres of walking trails in the conservation area, offering views of the 22-metre deep gorge.

The gorge is deep and the walls are steep. For your safety, only hike on marked trails. Stay away from the edge of the gorge. Do not climb over fences or attempt to climb down the gorge walls.

Nearby is the **[Elora Cataract Trailway](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/trails/elora-cataract-trailway/ "Elora Cataract Trailway")**, a 47-kilometre trail linking the Grand and Credit river watersheds.

[Cycling](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_7)

Cyclists can explore the **[Elora Cataract Trailway](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/trails/elora-cataract-trailway/ "Elora Cataract Trailway")**, a 47-kilometre trail linking the Grand and Credit river watersheds. Cyclists can also enjoy themselves on conservation area roads. Please obey the rules of the road and, for your safety, wear a helmet.

[Picnicking](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_8)

A multi-use picnic area is adjacent to the campground. Picnic tables are scattered around the conservation area and near the splash pad. For cooking purposes, day-use visitors may use barbecues in designated picnic areas. Never leave barbecues unattended, and please use extreme caution.

[Activities and Events](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_b18af775-43ad-47e9-98ec-0dbbf08f2b04_9)

There are no events scheduled at this time.

## Facilities

[Gatehouse](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_1)

This is the location of the community bulletin board, pay phone and a lost and found. It is the place to go to report any problems or concerns, to get further information about the conservation area. Firewood and ice is available to purchase.

[Washrooms](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_2)

Washrooms and showers are available in the campground area. Washrooms are also available in the picnic area. Vault toilets are located throughout the conservation area.

[Group Facilities](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_3)

There is one picnic pavilion available for rent for family reunions, company picnics and other events:

- The full Kay Marston Pavilion accommodates about 200 people and has washrooms. The pavilion can also be split into two sections and rented out separately, each half accommodating about 100 people.

More information is available on our [Group Facilities](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/conservation-area-services-info-fees-and-more/group-facilities/ "Group Facilities") page.

[Playgrounds and Sports Fields](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_4)

There is a playground for children, two baseball diamonds and large green spaces suitable for group games.

[Concession Stand](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_5)

The food concession stand offers hot food (hamburgers, french fries etc.), soft drinks and snacks.

[Dog Policy](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_6)

Dogs are welcome, but must be on a leash no longer than two-metres and under control at all times. Dogs are not allowed in the splash pad area. Please clean up after your dog. Pet owners may be fined if these regulations are not followed.

[Waste and Recycling](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_7)

Garbage containers are located throughout the conservation area and will be emptied as frequently as possible. However, people are reminded to visit responsibly and if garbage bins are full, to take their waste with them and dispose of it at home. Recycling bins are located in the campgrounds and at the dumping station. Please use the bins, as there is no collection from the campsites.

[Nearby Services](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_9f449ade-5933-4ac9-aebf-6ef9377417b8_8)

- Grocery, hardware and drug stores are in Elora and Fergus.
- Medical services are available at **[Groves Memorial Hospital](http://www.gmch.ca/ "Open new window to view Groves Memorial Hospital Page")**, 131 Frederick Campbell Street, Fergus.
- Visit the **[Elora & Fergus Tourism](http://www.grandandgorgeous.com/ "Open new window to view Elora & Fergus Tourism Page")** website for more information about the area.

Accessibility

[Facilities and Equipment](https://www.grandriver.ca/outdoor-recreation/conservation-areas/elora-gorge/#collapse_23613303-18fe-42b4-b550-29fe782b9029_1)

- The Kay Marston pavilion has an accessible access route, accessible picnic tables and an accessible washroom.
- The Northside washroom has an accessible exterior washroom and an accessible shower (no power-operated doors).
- The Pines washroom has an accessible exterior washroom and an accessible shower (no power-operated doors).
